account:
Today appears mostly routine so far. I read my appointment book this morning, attended office hours, and made the scheduled ten o'clock market walk. Several townsfolk had no news. Townsfolk 28, 18, and 08 all said the baker was carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. That could simply be supplies for baking; I have not seen it myself, and have no evidence of anything unusual behind it. I bought one fresh loaf for lunch. I saw the builder crossing the plaza carrying a lantern, but my question about town business apparently did not reach them before they walked away, so I learned nothing about their purpose.

The main unresolved matter is my fifteen hundred tea appointment, recorded only as 'Tea with the neighbour, dockside cottage (east bank).' The secretary initially had no confirmed host or cottage and asked about an invitation; I have no separate invitation. They later told me they were going to the east-bank cottages to identify the host and would report back. They have the appointment book with them. I heard them speaking again later but could not make out the words, so I do not know whether they have confirmed anything. This seems to be an effort to clarify my schedule, not evidence of any hidden activity.

It is now 11:09 and I am outside my home, early for noon lunch. I should keep the thirteen hundred office appointment for town accounts, seek the secretary's confirmation before three o'clock tea, return to the office at 16:30, and be home at nineteen hundred.
